'''Paul Reinhard Schimmel''' (born August 4, 1940) is an American biophysical chemist and translational medicine pioneer.

==Career==
Paul Schimmel is a Professor of Molecular Medicine<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.scripps.edu/research/faculty/schimmel|title=TSRI Faculty Page|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=}}</ref> at The [[Scripps Research]] Institute. Prior to joining The Scripps Research Institute, he was a John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Professor of Biochemistry and Biophysics at MIT ([[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]). Author or coauthor of many scientific research publications,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/myncbi/paul.schimmel.1/bibliography/public/?sortby=pubDate&sdirection=ascending|title=Complete List of Published Work in MyBibliography|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=}}</ref> he is also coauthor of a widely used 3-volume textbook on biophysical chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.macmillanlearning.com/Catalog/product/biophysicalchemistry-firstedition-cantor/tableofcontents#tab|title=Biophysical Chemistry Part I: The Conformation of Biological Macromolecules, Biophysical Chemistry Part II: Techniques for the Study of Biological Structure and Function, Biophysical Chemistry Part III: The Behavior of Biological Macromolecules|last1=Cantor|first1=Charles R.|authorlink=|last2=Schimmel|first2=Paul R.|authorlink2=|date=|website=Macmillan Learning|access-date=}}</ref> His research interests have focused on aminoacyl tRNA synthetases as fundamental interpreters of the genetic information.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.scripps.edu/schimmel/|title=Schimmel Lab Website|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=}}</ref> Through career-long investigations of this ancient and universal set of essential enzymes, his laboratory has worked on a universal mechanism for correcting errors in the interpretation of genetic information,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Schmidt|first1=E.|last2=Schimmel|first2=P.|date=April 8, 1994|title=Mutational isolation of a sieve for editing in a transfer RNA synthetase|journal=Science|volume=264|issue=5156|pages=265–267|issn=0036-8075|pmid=8146659|doi=10.1126/science.8146659|bibcode=1994Sci...264..265S }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Song|first1=Youngzee|last2=Zhou|first2=Huihao|last3=Vo|first3=My-Nuong|last4=Shi|first4=Yi|last5=Nawaz|first5=Mir Hussain|last6=Vargas-Rodriguez|first6=Oscar|last7=Diedrich|first7=Jolene K.|last8=Yates|first8=John R.|last9=Kishi|first9=Shuji|date=December 22, 2017|title=Double mimicry evades tRNA synthetase editing by toxic vegetable-sourced non-proteinogenic amino acid|journal=Nature essential for maintaining cellular homeostasis and for preventing serious pathologies and disease.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lee|first1=Jeong Woong|last2=Beebe|first2=Kirk|last3=Nangle|first3=Leslie A.|last4=Jang|first4=Jaeseon|last5=Longo-Guess|first5=Chantal M.|last6=Cook|first6=Susan A.|last7=Davisson|first7=Muriel T.|last8=Sundberg|first8=John P.|last9=Schimmel|first9=Paul|date=September 7, His laboratory also discovered what others have referred to as a tRNA synthetase-directed primordial, or 'second', genetic code that eventually was incorporated into the modern code.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Francklyn|first1=C.|last2=Schimmel|first2=P.|date=February 2, 1989|title=Aminoacylation of RNA minihelices with alanine|journal=Nature|volume=337|issue=6206|pages=478–481|doi=10.1038/337478a0|issn=0028-0836|pmid=2915692|bibcode=1989Natur.337..478F |s2cid=4268171}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Francklyn|first1=C.|last2=Shi|first2=J. P.|last3=Schimmel|first3=P.|date=February 28, 1992|title=Overlapping nucleotide determinants for specific aminoacylation of RNA microhelices|journal=Science|volume=255|issue=5048|pages=1121–1125|issn=0036-8075|pmid=1546312|doi=10.1126/science.1546312|bibcode=1992Sci...255.1121F }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Schimmel|first=Paul|date=January 2018|title=The emerging complexity of the tRNA world: mammalian tRNAs beyond protein synthesis|journal=Nature Reviews. Molecular Cell Biology|volume=19|issue=1|pages=45–58|doi=10.1038/nrm.2017.77|issn=1471-0080|pmid=28875994|s2cid=5231605}}</ref> In a separate line of research published back in 1983, Schimmel developed the concept of what are now known as ESTs (expressed sequence tags) and the strategy of shotgun sequencing, approaches that several years later were adopted for the human genome project.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Putney|first1=S. D.|last2=Herlihy|first2=W. C.|last3=Schimmel|first3=P.|date=April 21, 1983|title=A new troponin T and cDNA clones for 13 different muscle proteins, found by shotgun sequencing|journal=Nature|volume=302|issue=5910|pages=718–721|issn=0028-0836|pmid=6687628|doi=10.1038/302718a0|bibcode=1983Natur.302..718P |s2cid=4364361}}</ref> Nature magazine listed Schimmel's work on the development of ESTs as one of the four key developments that launched the human genome project.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lander|first1=E. S.|last2=Linton|first2=L. M.|last3=Birren|first3=B.|last4=Nusbaum|first4=C.|last5=Zody|first5=M. C.|last6=Baldwin|first6=J.|last7=Devon|first7=K.|last8=Dewar|first8=K.|last9=Doyle|first9=M.|date=February 15, 2001|title=Initial sequencing and analysis of the human genome|journal=Nature|volume=409|issue=6822|pages=860–921|doi=10.1038/35057062|issn=0028-0836|pmid=11237011|url=https://deepblue.lib.umich.edu/bitstream/2027.42/62798/1/409860a0.pdf|doi-access=free}}</ref>  Lastly, his laboratory established connections of synthetases to disease and, most recently, they reported the structural and functional metamorphosis of these proteins, whereby they are repurposed with novel activities, both inside and outside the cell, in a variety of cell signaling pathways<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Guo|first1=Min|last2=Schimmel|first2=Paul|date=March 2013|title=Essential nontranslational functions of tRNA synthetases|journal=Nature Chemical Biology|volume=9|issue=3|pages=145–153|doi=10.1038/nchembio.1158|pmc=3773598|pmid=23416400}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sajish|first1=Mathew|last2=Schimmel|first2=Paul|date=March 19, 2015|title=A human tRNA synthetase is a potent PARP1-activating effector target for resveratrol|journal=Nature|volume=519|issue=7543|pages=370–373|doi=10.1038/nature14028|pmc=4368482|pmid=25533949|bibcode=2015Natur.519..370S }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lo|first1=Wing-Sze|last2=Gardiner|first2=Elisabeth|last3=Xu|first3=Zhiwen|last4=Lau|first4=Ching-Fun|last5=Wang|first5=Feng|last6=Zhou|first6=Jie J.|last7=Mendlein|first7=John D.|last8=Nangle|first8=Leslie A.|last9=Chiang|first9=Kyle P.|date=July 18, 2014|title=Human tRNA synthetase catalytic nulls with diverse functions|journal=Science|volume=345|issue=6194|pages=328–332|doi=10.1126/science.1252943|pmc=4188629|pmid=25035493|bibcode=2014Sci...345..328L }}</ref>

== Honors ==
Named to various society and university awards and honorary degrees, and elected to membership in the American Academy of Arts and Sciences,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/peerCollaboration/profile.aspx?c=psa&q=paul_Schimmel|title=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=}}</ref> the National Academy of Sciences,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/paul-r-schimmel-hrpueq/|title=National Academy of Sciences|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=}}</ref> the American Philosophical Society,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Paul+Schimmel&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced|title=American Philosophical Society|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=}}</ref> the Institute of Medicine (National Academy of Medicine)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nam.edu/directory/?lastName=Schimmel&firstName=Paul&parentInstitution=&yearStart=&yearEnd=&presence=1|title=National Academy of Medicine|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=}}</ref> and National Academy of Inventors.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.academyofinventors.org|title=National Academy of Inventors|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=}}</ref> Active in many scientific and academic organizations and committees, including past service as President of the Division of Biological Chemistry of the American Chemical Society (presently with over 7,000 members) and as an editorial board member of numerous scientific journals. In June 2020, he was named the 2020 winner of the [[Kathryn Hach-Darrow|Kathryn C. Hach]] Award for Entrepreneurial Success for "co-founding more than ten biotech companies and aiding others in their endeavors for nearly three decades."<ref>{{Cite web|title=2020 National Award Recipients Citations|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/recipients/2019-national-award-recipients-citations1.html|access-date=June 13, 2020|website=American Chemical Society|language=en}}</ref> Named the ARCS San Diego Chapter 2020 Scientist of the Year<ref>{{Cite web|title=ARCS 2020 Scientist of the Year {{!}} San Diego|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rLZlvgHypIA|access-date=April 17, 2021|website=san-diego.arcsfoundation.org| date=September 28, 2020 }}</ref>
